events.label: WTI weekly settlement — formal $80 trip wire; NFLX AH overhang opens Friday
events.note: WTI intraday-breached $80 for the second consecutive session (July 15 and July 16) but settled below the trigger both times (~$79.85 and ~$79.63 respectively). A Friday settlement above $80 is the formal trip wire that converts STEP ASIDE to BEARISH check and mandates XLE escalation to 15%. A settlement below $79 would partially relieve the two-day intraday breach pattern. Low volume positioning day; NFLX Q3 guidance miss (revenue $12.86B vs $13.01B est) weighs on consumer tech at the open.

events.label: PayPal (PYPL) board response to Stripe/Advent $60.50/share (~$53B) acquisition bid
events.note: Stripe and Advent International jointly bid $60.50/share (~$53B total enterprise value) on July 16 to acquire PayPal. PYPL surged +18% on the announcement. Board is expected to formally respond by July 20. Combined entity would process an estimated $3.7 trillion in annual payment volume. Deal-spread arbitrage active; Polymarket 82% deal-close probability. DOJ antitrust risk on Stripe-PayPal combination is the primary deal-break scenario. If board responds positively, deal-arb spread narrows and PYPL may rerate toward $60+ range.

events.label: TSLA Q2 2026 earnings (after close) + IBM full Q2 earnings call + GOOGL Q2 earnings (after close) — triple clearing event
events.note: TSLA: Q2 earnings follow the blowout July 2 delivery report (480K vs 406K consensus). Need gross margin recovery (>25%, from sub-15% in Q1) and FSD revenue recognition at scale for re-rate above $420. IBM: full Q2 call gives context on the software-to-hardware budget rotation that caused IBM's -25% worst day on record July 14. CEO must clarify: one-quarter or multi-year? GOOGL Q2: AI Overviews monetization, Search share vs AI competitors, and capex trajectory are the market-moving variables. Triple-report Wednesday is the largest single earnings day remaining in Q2 — sets the tone heading into FOMC week.

events.label: AMD AI Day — San Francisco (Jul 22-23) — MI400 roadmap, competitive positioning vs NVDA
events.note: AMD's annual AI event in San Francisco runs July 22-23. First major deep-dive on the MI400 series roadmap since Computex. UBS raised AMD PT to $700, Rosenblatt to $665. AMD closed at $529.14 (–3.46%) on July 16 on TSMC wafer hike impact. The event could be a re-rating catalyst if AMD provides hyperscaler win disclosures and competitive NVDA pricing commentary. Context: NVDA staged a dramatic intraday recovery on July 16 from $197 premarket to ~$208-210 close — NVDA's relative AI positioning strength makes AMD's AI Day case harder to make. Do not add AMD above $530 ahead of the event.

events.label: FOMC meeting (Jul 28-29) — July hike probability ~20%; September language is the critical signal
events.note: July hike base case remains no-hike (~20% probability). The September language in the FOMC statement and dot-plot update is the market-moving variable. September hike probability has risen from 44.5% (pre-July 15 CPI/PPI prints) to approximately 58% as of July 16 close — driven entirely by WTI double-testing $80 intraday and Iran Hormuz blockade loading into August CPI. If Warsh's dot-plot signals September hike clearly: 30Y re-accelerates, IWM headwinds worsen, BUY conditions pushed back to post-August CPI. If dots hold September in question: rate relief window opens.

events.label: META Q2 2026 earnings — AI cloud business first quantification; peak Q2 earnings week (MSFT, AMZN also)
events.note: META Q2 earnings July 29 is the first event where management must quantify the AI cloud business (Bloomberg July 1: Meta building AI cloud to sell excess compute). MSFT and AMZN also report in late July — peak Q2 earnings risk window. IBM's enterprise software warning (July 14) adds a risk factor for MSFT Azure enterprise consulting revenue. META's ad-driven model is insulated from IBM's enterprise IT budget rotation. GOOGL reports July 22 (earlier than prior, in the triple-event session).

events.label: July CPI release (est. Aug 13) — captures WTI $80 double-test (Jul 15-16) + Iran Hormuz blockade oil pass-through
events.note: June CPI (July 14) captured pre-Hormuz-shock prices and printed -0.4% MoM / 3.5% YoY. July CPI will be the FIRST month to reflect the WTI +9.4% spike of July 13 and the ongoing Strait disruption. WTI has now intraday-breached $80 for two consecutive sessions (July 15-16), settling just below the trip wire both times. Even at $79.63 settlement, the July 13-16 WTI range represents a significant positive energy contribution to July CPI. 30Y above 5.00% for five consecutive sessions is the bond market front-running August CPI. September hike probability at 58% and approaching 60% formal trigger.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — $91B revenue guide; AI capex cycle fundamental clearing event
events.note: NVDA's Q2 FY27 earnings is the fundamental clearing event for the AI capex thesis. $91B revenue guidance represents sequential acceleration. TSMC Q2 (July 16) confirmed the AI demand thesis with $40.2B revenue and FY guidance raised to >40% USD — and TSMC's supply shortage for N3/N5 nodes extending into 2027 is demand-bullish. However, the 5-10% wafer price hike across ALL advanced nodes (including 5nm, NVDA's primary manufacturing node) introduces a 2-4pp gross margin headwind that management must address on the August 26 call. NVDA demonstrated exceptional relative strength July 16 — recovering from $197 premarket to ~$208-210 close despite SMH –4% — signaling the market views NVDA's AI positioning as insulated from commodity-chip selloff. Full-size add gate: sustained close above $210 + wafer hike impact clarified + VIX below 15.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since June 12 IPO. SPCX touched an intraday all-time low of $132.75 on July 15 (below $135 IPO price) — down 30%+ from June 16 ATH of $225.64. 27 of 31 analysts still carry Buy ratings; the sell-side downgrade cycle has barely begun. December 2026 lock-up expiry adds supply overhang. Re-entry gate: first earnings print (Starlink ARR growth, Starship launch cadence, cash burn) is the fundamental clearing event. Net losses are structural ($4.9B in 2025, $4.28B in Q1 2026). Better entry $115-120 for risk-tolerant 12-month investors.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs. The $20B bond offering (June 22) already changed the capital structure risk profile — the lock-up expiry adds equity supply overhang.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off -13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst and adds uncertainty to AI infrastructure spending trajectories.
